findings.quote: That the two ways of steadying a tower differ less in what they deliver at handover than in what becomes of it later.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick B): A reduces a main-idea answer to an anecdote about tourists plus the overclaim that the machine has stopped earning its keep, and D names a different subject entirely (underestimated wind loads, revised margins). That leaves the hedged comparative B against the one-sided C, which form alone does not decide - an opinion piece could legitimately key to C.

findings.quote: They fell as the buildings took on partitions and equipment, moving away from the settings the dampers had been given.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick D): adding mass lowers a structure's natural frequency, so D is reachable from first-year structural dynamics, and C is D's absolute twin (each of the nineteen, a full seven percent). A and B remain substantive positions, so the passage still does real work.

findings.quote: Rask says that a shape is tuned as well, though not to a frequency. What does the text suggest follows from this?
findings.note: PARTIALLY with a stem-entailment component: the stem supplies the premise that a shape is tuned to something other than a frequency, which pushes toward the surroundings reading in C. B contradicts the premise the stem sets up and D is a zoning prescription rather than a consequence, so only A and C survive blind.

findings.quote: He grants Marek that a shape outlasts its owners, while denying that this is what makes it the safer choice.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick A): an attitude stem with two eliminable extremes - C is full endorsement and D is full dismissal (a designer's vanity entirely discredited). A and B both survive, but A is the only concessive-plus-qualification shape, which is the usual key form for this stem type.

findings.quote: Its weight: a plug door of that period was far heavier than the square door it replaced, and heavier than the tools of the day could shift.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick B): A carries an absolute a passage would have to prove twice over (heavier than the tools of the day could shift), and C and D make overlapping roundness-distributes-force claims that cannot both be keys, which narrows to B. Against that, B is the only option that does not appeal to the door being round, a counter-tell, so form alone does not settle it.

findings.quote: To show that water can look blue where there is no sky to reflect and no colored surface to borrow from.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick C): water is intrinsically blue through red-end absorption and the standard demonstration is exactly a white-lined indoor pool, so a reader who knows the physics picks C without the text. B and D are substantive real misconceptions (lining color, dissolved substances) that a passage would have to rule out, so this is normal comprehension work rather than a leak.

findings.quote: Ju noggrannare en sträcka hade rensats, desto fler rensningsdagar krävde den, oberoende av hur brant fallet var.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick B): C is B's absolute twin, adding the unqualified oberoende av hur brant fallet var, and D answers a question about efterrensning with a claim that brötarna took most of the season. A and B remain substantive opposite-direction readings of the same record, so the passage is still needed.

findings.quote: Att timmer som låg kvar på annans strand skulle vara bortfört senast den femtonde september.
findings.note: Cross-question leak rather than an in-stem one: within q:2 the four statutory duties are indistinguishable blind, but option C of q:3 (fristen den femtonde september) presupposes exactly the deadline D states, corroborating D from the question set alone without any passage.

findings.quote: Eftersom det bärgade timret hade ett gott värde kunde föreningen utan vidare räkna hem kostnaden för de sena utryckningarna.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick A): B carries an unearned absolute (utan vidare räkna hem kostnaden) and C another (upphörde helt så snart fristen hade löpt ut), both reading as overclaims for an inference stem. A and D both hedge with tycks, so the hedge tell does not single A out and the key is not decided blind.

findings.quote: Dagsverksböckerna visar entydigt att brötarbetet saknade betydelse för hur flottningen organiserades i Vitmyrbygden.
findings.note: PARTIALLY: D is the absolute overclaim (entydigt, saknade betydelse) and A makes a causal claim about when the whole flottningsepok ended that is far larger than a dagsverksbok can support. B and C both remain plausible best-fit statements, so two eliminations but no decision.

findings.quote: Bemannade skolbibliotek höjde både utlåningen och det källkritiska arbetet på samtliga stadier som ingick i de fyra kommunerna.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick C): D states a causal effect with an absolute scope (höjde, samtliga stadier) that no such survey could deliver, and A is C with the arrow reversed. A stays substantive as a reverse-causation finding, so form alone narrows to A versus C without deciding.

findings.quote: Att pengarna gick till böcker och hyllor när det som saknades var någon som kunde arbeta med samlingen.
findings.note: Cross-question leak: taken alone the four critiques are not separable blind (A is only a generic more-money complaint), but q:1 of the same set establishes the staffed-librarian finding across three of its four options, and B is the only critique that follows from it. The pair is answerable without the passage.

findings.quote: Klagomålen på lösa hundar upphörde helt i alla parker där en inhägnad hade anlagts under de två åren.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick A): D is an absolute (upphörde helt, alla parker) no inventory would report, and B is A with the causal arrow reversed. B still stands as a substantive confound finding and C as a substantive displacement finding, so the eliminations narrow the field without settling it.

findings.quote: Frågan om hundrastgårdar handlar mindre om antalet än om var de placeras och för vem.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick D): A is a prescriptive absolute (bör inte byggas, bara flyttar sig), C generalises to urban densification which no dog-run inventory supports, and D is the sole hedged comparative of the shape this stem type usually keys to. B survives as a real possible headline result, and q:1 of the same set independently points at placement, so the pick leans on the question set rather than on the passage.
